.qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-02-r10/task/tests/scored/polish/judge.toml and scored/visual/judge.toml (parsed: criterion counts, weights, types)
evidence: Policy: task/tests/scoring.toml:1-3 has [gates] render = 0.0, constraints = 0.0; :5-8 weights functional 0.6 / polish 0.2 / visual 0.2 (sum 1.0, no gate name in [weights]); :10-11 [floors] functional = 0.05. scoring.toml, test.sh and tools/score.py are byte-identical to the frozen template (sha256 95f70d6e..., bd682592..., 13de2b38... on both sides), so the task did not alter shared reward policy. Order: test.sh:213 runs the gates suite first; :216-222 runs score.py and on exit 1 (real gate failure) exits before test.sh:224 ever starts the scored suite; any other non-zero exit writes the plain zero. score.py:40-41 gates pass only when every gate score > 0.0; :42-44 scored dimensions are forced to 0.0 unless gates passed and scored data exists; :46 the weighted mean iterates only over [weights], so gate scores contribute no mass; :47-48 reward is 0.0 unless gates AND floors pass; :83 returns 1 on gate failure. Gate judge.toml files use aggregation all_pass with binary criteria (render 1 criterion, constraints 2) and carry no weight key in [judge]. Executed locally (frozen score.py against synthetic suite outputs written to a scratch directory, no task files touched): render 0 / constraints 1 with a perfect scored file -> exit 1, reward 0.0, all scored dims 0; render 1 / constraints 0 -> exit 1, reward 0.0; gates pass with functional 0.05, polish 1, visual 1 -> reward 0.0, floors_passed 0 (strict >, weighted_score 0.43 not paid); functional 0.0 with polish/visual 1 -> reward 0.0; functional 0.06 -> 0.436; all 1.0 -> 1.0 (gates add nothing); gate file missing a dimension -> exit 2 -> plain zero path. Floor arithmetic for this task: functional has 42 binary criteria, total weight 58.5, largest single weight 2.0 (0.0342), so no single criterion clears the 0.05 floor; more than 2.925 weight is needed. A minimal app that only satisfies the gates (custom non-editable editor surface that takes typing plus server-backed save) can at most collect cw_save_reload_restart (1.5) and cw_long_line_editing (1.0) = 2.5/58.5 = 0.0427 < 0.05 without implementing further real behaviour, so its polish/visual points are zeroed. Every other functional criterion needs a real additional capability (undo, selection, Run, find, history, live updates) and most carry a positive control. Actual-run evidence (earlier candidate, not these bytes): raw-evidence-index artifact hashes for the GPT-5.6 Luna trial verified (result.json abbf4ace..., gates/reward-details.json 617e450f...); its verifier/reward.json shows render 0.0, constraints 1.0, reward 0.0, gates_passed 0, and no verifier/scored directory exists, i.e. a failed gate zeroed the reward and the scored suite was skipped by the same test.sh/score.py logic. Residual risk (why risk=true): no configured judge run exists for these exact bytes, and no weak-app run that passes both gates has been measured, so the floor behaviour on a real gate-passing weak app is established by code execution and arithmetic only, not by a verifier run. The gap between the gate-only ceiling (0.0427) and the floor (0.05) is narrow: one further low-weight functional pass crosses it and unlocks up to 0.4 of polish/visual. That is the frozen template floor value and is not a task defect, but it is unmeasured here.
